## Acceptance criteria (README M1)

- Target: Hindi ≥ 15% and Hinglish ≥ 10% fewer tokens than the byte-level BPE baseline.
- **Result: NOT MET by any candidate at comparable vocabulary.**

### `sp_bpe` vs `byte_bpe` @ requested 1024 (actual 1024 vs 1024)

| slice | baseline tokens | challenger tokens | reduction | comparable |
|---|---:|---:|---:|:--:|
| Hindi (Devanagari) | 5608 | 4053 | +27.7% | ✅ |
| English (Latin) | 4256 | 4278 | -0.5% | ✅ |
| Hinglish (romanized, code-mixed) | 3442 | 3444 | -0.1% | ✅ |
| Mixed-script Hinglish (Devanagari + Latin words) | 5587 | 4156 | +25.6% | ✅ |
| Constructed code-switch stress slice | 8982 | 7711 | +14.2% | ✅ |

- Hindi (Devanagari): measured +27.7% vs target +15% → **✅ PASS** — provisional slice
- Hinglish (romanized, code-mixed): measured -0.1% vs target +10% → **❌ FAIL** — provisional slice
  - why it failed: a byte-level BPE trained on this corpus already merges the Latin-script words that dominate romanized Hinglish, so the Devanagari byte penalty that BPE suffers does not apply to this slice

## Selection

Measured winner on the India-relevant slices: **`sp_bpe` at vocabulary 2048**.
Basis: no candidate met all acceptance criteria; this is the fewest-tokens-on-India-slices candidate, reported for information only.
Eligible to be called a release tokenizer: **no**.
- corpus is 171476 chars (< 1000000); metrics are pipeline-validation only
- corpus is a composed fixture, not natural text (see data/manifests/sources.yaml)

## How to read this without over-claiming

- These are measurements of *subword mechanics* on the stated corpus. They say nothing about
  model quality, Hindi fluency, or SIR's capabilities.
- If a criterion failed, the failure is the result. The criterion stays as written; a future
  run must beat it on a licensed corpus.
- `chars/token` is reported for comparability, but the number that changes training cost is
  total tokens for the same text, which is what the acceptance test uses.
